"You have to show what I said to reality so that the players believe and follow you. No matter how good the story is, if there is no result, who will follow it?"
The core of the leadership emphasized by Kim Ki-dong (54), who led FC Seoul to the top of the K League 1 for the first time in 10 years this season, was "proof." Rather than forcing one's philosophy, the leader must show the fact that the philosophy is right on the field to gain the trust of the players.
Coach Kim said in an interview with Maeil Business on the 16th, "I will explain my tactics and strategies to the players and trust and follow the coach next time if it fits in the actual game and comes out well," adding, "True leadership is to prove it with results and contents, not words."
Coach Kim, who has led Seoul since 2024, won 67 points (20 wins, 7 draws and 8 losses) this year after ranking fourth in the K League 1 in his first year in office and sixth last year, confirming an early victory and cheering. He, who earned the modifier "iron man" by playing 501 K-League games during his active days, became the coach of the national soccer team under the age of 23 and Pohang coach in 2019 and took over as head coach of Pohang. Coach Kim, who has already been a professional coach for eight years, gave meaning, saying, "I think the stepping stone has been established to move forward for another goal in the future by winning my first K League 1 championship as a coach."
Above all, it came more meaningful because it was a victory created by the leadership change that head coach Kim himself tried. During his time with the Pohang Steelers, he achieved results through strong training and strict guidance, but in Seoul, he changed his approach. This is because there are many star players and the size and culture of the club were different. Coach Kim said, "I reduced the amount of training by nearly half as much as I did in Pohang, and I thought about how to make it on my side while respecting the players."
He has also changed the way he communicates with players. I don't immediately reprimand him for losing the game. Wait for the emotion to subside and watch the video together a day or two later to point out the problem. They also work hard to discover advantages before players' shortcomings and maximize them.
The change in leadership style led to a change in team culture. Before head coach Kim took office, Seoul had a strong tendency for some star players to lead the team's atmosphere. However, through the reorganization of the squad over three years, we have created a culture where everyone sacrifices for the team without relying on specific players. Coach Kim said, "The team changed as the new players accepted the coach's football philosophy and delivered it to their juniors."
It's not just that the past three years have been smooth for head coach Kim. In particular, last year, due to poor performance and various controversies surrounding the club, fans were strongly booed by Kim Ki-dong. After the end of last year's season, he even received a proposal to move to another team, but manager Kim refused. He said, "If you leave the team at that time, you will run away. If I go out like that, I thought the stigma would continue to follow me," he said, looking back, "I decided to leave well with results here." Instead of avoiding criticism, he was determined to prove his football. In the end, he turned the booing toward him into praise, putting Seoul at the top of the list for the first time in a year.
The growth of individual players was also noticeable. Captain Kim Jin-soo succeeded in expanding his role, which was limited to the side, to the center through constant video analysis, and striker Moon Seon-min also improved his concentration and performance. Klimala, a foreign main scorer, also transformed into a different player than before by joining the defense and learning the linked play.
Coach Kim waved his hands to evaluate the change as a commonly called "motor magic." He said, "There is no magic. It's just a price of effort, he said with strength, "I don't see luck, but I believe it comes to those who try."
Coach Kim's challenge, which put Seoul at the top, is now at a new starting line. He stressed that continuing the championship is a more difficult task. Coach Kim said, "The true reputation is not a team that wins once and falls again. Even if we don't win, we should be in the top three every year and be able to challenge for the top again next season, he said. "A team that consistently maintains the top ranks can lead the K-League."
For this, the support of the club and the strengthening of the player base should be supported. Coach Kim said, "We can't change everything at once, but it's possible if we set the direction and develop it little by little with the club."
What head coach Kim ultimately pursues is not just winning soccer, but soccer that gives joy and emotion to fans. As such, director Kim himself promised constant change as a leader. "In the future, I want to continue to grow as a leader while developing more details," he said.
[Reporter Kim Jihan]
